title: What to Watch This Week: Alia Bhatt Picks Up a Gun, Rajkumar Hirani Finally Comes to Streaming, and Enola Holmes Gets Married
excerpt: Alpha storms theatres on July 3, Pritam and Pedro marks Hirani's OTT debut on JioHotstar, and Netflix drops both Enola Holmes 3 and a Legally Blonde prequel — your streaming-and-cinema guide for June 29 to July 5.
body:
The half-year mark just landed, and the entertainment gods have apparently decided to throw everything at you at once. Between the biggest Bollywood theatrical event of the summer, a legendary filmmaker's long-awaited streaming debut, and Netflix treating July 1 like a second Christmas, your week is about to get very full. Here's what deserves your time — and what you can skip dinner for.

## 1. Alpha — Theatres, July 3

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>


**Why it matters:** The YRF Spy Universe finally gets its first female-led chapter, and it's built around two of the most electrifying women in Hindi cinema right now. **Alia Bhatt** plays a girl named Sita, raised from childhood as a weapon. **Sharvari** — fresh off the lethal energy she brought to *Vedaa* and *Munjya* — joins her as the second operative. **Bobby Deol** plays the villain. **Anil Kapoor** shows up in a pivotal role. The trailer is all shattered glass, point-blank kills, and Alia looking like she hasn't smiled in three years. It's gorgeous.

Directed by **Shiv Rawail** (*The Railway Men*) and produced by **Aditya Chopra**, this one has been pushed back three times — from Christmas 2025 to April to July — because the VFX apparently needed to be flawless. The advance buzz suggests it was worth the wait. If you're watching from the US, UK, or Canada, it's getting a wide international release on day one.

**The verdict:** The most anticipated Bollywood release of the summer. Don't wait for OTT on this one — it's made for IMAX.

## 2. Pritam and Pedro — JioHotstar, July 3

**Why it matters:** **Rajkumar Hirani** — the man behind *3 Idiots*, *PK*, and the *Munna Bhai* films — is finally making his streaming debut. And he's bringing **Arshad Warsi**, his original Circuit, along for the ride. The series is a cybercrime comedy-thriller set in Goa, pairing **Vir Hirani** (Rajkumar's son, making his acting debut as Pritam) with Warsi's Inspector Pedro Gonsalves.



> **"Elle Season 1 — Prime Video, July 1

Before Harvard Law, before "What, like it's hard?" — there was high school in 1990s Seattle."**


The cast is absurd: **Vikrant Massey** as the antagonist Martin, **Boman Irani** in a pivotal role, **Mona Singh**, and — if Arshad Warsi's loose lips at the trailer launch are to be believed — a **Sanjay Dutt** cameo. Hirani told press the idea came from actual Mumbai Cyber Cell cases during the lockdown. The writing team includes **Abhijat Joshi**, who co-wrote *3 Idiots* and *PK*.

> "Where data meets danda, chaos meets confusion" — that's how the makers describe it, and honestly, that's the most Hirani sentence ever written.

**Diaspora access:** JioHotstar is available in the US, UK, and Canada. If you have a subscription, this is your Thursday night sorted.

## 3. Enola Holmes 3 — Netflix, July 1


![Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d6/YRF_Spy_Universe_logo.jpg)


**Millie Bobby Brown** is back as the youngest Holmes sibling, and this time the plot is deliciously personal: she's preparing for her wedding to Lord Tewkesbury (**Louis Partridge**) in Malta when Dr. Watson shows up with the news that her brother **Sherlock** (**Henry Cavill**) has been kidnapped. So she does what any Holmes would do — abandons the ceremony and goes hunting.

Directed by **Philip Barantini** (who made the single-take restaurant thriller *Boiling Point*), the third instalment promises higher stakes and more action. Helena Bonham Carter returns as Eudoria Holmes. It's light, it's clever, and it's the kind of thing you can watch with your whole family without anyone checking their phone.

## 4. Elle Season 1 — Prime Video, July 1

Before Harvard Law, before "What, like it's hard?" — there was high school in 1990s Seattle. **Elle** is the *Legally Blonde* prequel series nobody asked for but everyone's going to binge. Produced by **Reese Witherspoon** herself and starring newcomer **Lexi Minetree** as the teenage Elle Woods, the show traces how an ordinary girl in flannel-era Seattle starts becoming the pink-clad force of nature we know. Already renewed for Season 2 before the first episode drops.

## 5. Silo Season 3 — Apple TV+, July 3

**Rebecca Ferguson** returns to the bunker. After last season's devastating finale, Juliette finds herself back home with no memory of what happened. The dystopian sci-fi series — based on Hugh Howey's novels — has quietly become one of the best shows on any platform, and Season 3 promises to finally crack open the backstory of the silos themselves. If you haven't started *Silo* yet, you've got two days to catch up. It's worth the sprint.

## 6. Half Man — Lionsgate Play, July 3

The creator of *Baby Reindeer* is back. **Richard Gadd** writes and stars in this HBO drama alongside **Jamie Bell**, exploring toxic masculinity across thirty years through the relationship between two men bound by brotherhood and a past that won't let go. If *Baby Reindeer* left you shattered, this will too — Gadd doesn't do comfortable. Available in India on Lionsgate Play.

## 7. Welcome to the Jungle — Theatres (Still Running)

If you haven't caught it yet, **Akshay Kumar's** comedy juggernaut has crossed **₹50 crore** in three days and is looking at a weekend total north of ₹65 crore. The audience word-of-mouth is strong, Sunday occupancy is climbing, and it's the kind of undemanding, belly-laugh Bollywood that plays beautifully in a packed house. Grab the tickets before Alpha steals its screens on Thursday.

---

**Honourable mentions:** *Dark Winds* Season 4 lands on Netflix July 4 for those who like their crime procedurals set on Navajo land. *Isakapatnam*, a Telugu power-struggle thriller starring Samuthirakani and Aishwarya Rajesh, hits Prime Video July 3. And *Cocktail 2* is still holding strong in its second weekend at **₹134 crore worldwide** — catch it if the rom-com itch hasn't been scratched.

This might be the most stacked week of the year. Set your alarms, clear your evenings, and for the love of Hirani — don't let any of this go to your watchlist graveyard.
